fixed.red: On unchanged code at origin/main 88e55be, the test seeds two matches: the fixture's draft return ACC-PINV-2026-00020 against BILL, and a draft purchase invoice ACC-PINV-2026-00009 of SUPP-0001 with bill_no CN-77 (the credit_note helper). It then calls create_draft_purchase_return with bill_no CN-77 and no allow_duplicate. Command: uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py -k matching_twice. It failed on the assertion of the refusal's full text: the actual text was "...exists (ACC-PINV-2026-00020). Check it first; ..." and the expected text was "...exists (ACC-PINV-2026-00020), and a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no exists (ACC-PINV-2026-00009). Check them first; ...". The test also checks that erp.writes() == []. After the fix it passes, and the full suite (1576 tests), ruff check, ruff format, basedpyright and mdformat are all green.
fixed.notes: The branch did not exist yet, so I started it from origin/main. Fix: drafts.refuse_matches builds a single refusal from every Match, joined with ", and ", and says "Check them first" when there are several. drafts.refuse_duplicates now calls it with one match, so the single-match text is unchanged for every other create. returns.create raises refuse_matches(found) where it used to pass found[0] alone. There is a CHANGELOG line under Unreleased/Fixed. Only tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py, src/enterich/tools/drafts.py, src/enterich/tools/returns.py and CHANGELOG.md changed.

problems: tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py (new test test_a_debit_note_matching_twice_is_refused_naming_both, around line 1107) writes the whole refusal inline, including both kinds and matches ('draft return' / 'invoice (return_against)', 'purchase invoice' / 'supplier and bill_no') and the closing sentence. Its neighbours build these texts with the shared Duplicate helper: BY_INVOICE.refusal(...) at line 544, BY_BILL.refusal(...) at line 1096, with the constants at lines 34-35. tests/integration/duplicates.py's docstring makes that module the one place that writes out the duplicate texts 'for every draft's tests'. Because the test bypasses it, the kind/match wording now lives in two places in the tests, and a change to BY_INVOICE or BY_BILL would not reach this test. The fix gave src a multi-match form (drafts.refuse_matches) but added nothing matching to tests/integration/duplicates.py. Suggested fix: write a multi-match refusal out in tests/integration/duplicates.py, for example a function taking (Duplicate, found) pairs that joins the clauses with ', and ' and says 'Check them first'. Have Duplicate.refusal stay the one-match case. Then call it from the new test with BY_INVOICE/PURCHASE_DRAFT and BY_BILL/'ACC-PINV-2026-00009'.
review.reason:
I read the finding from 9eebe8b:harness/runs/2026-11-20-code/fixes.jsonl. It says returns.create refused with found[0] alone, against REQ-001-PRS-F005 ('naming the matching documents') and REQ-005-PRS-F009. I then read diff 6afd004^..195f5ef. Red/green, redone in a detached worktree in the scratchpad: at 6afd004 the new test fails on the full-text assertion; the actual text ends '...(ACC-PINV-2026-00020). Check it first; ...' and the expected text names ACC-PINV-2026-00009 too. At 195f5ef the whole of tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py passes (116 tests). The worktree is removed.

The test itself is sound. It seeds both matches: the fixture's draft return PURCHASE_DRAFT and credit_note(erp, status='Draft'). It goes through the MCP tool, asserts the full refusal text and erp.writes() == [], so it checks what the finding says is missing, through behaviour a caller sees. It does not repeat an existing test. It sits beside its neighbours in the 'credit note number (REQ-005-PRS-F009)' section.

The code change stays inside the specs:
- drafts.refuse_duplicates now delegates to the new refuse_matches, and the single-match text is byte-identical.
- returns.py:235 is the only call site changed.
- The other creates (procure_to_pay.py:356, order_to_cash.py:286, bank_and_cash.py:505, record_to_report.py:585) keep their single match.
- The CHANGELOG has a line under Unreleased/Fixed.
- Nothing else changed beyond the finding.

One thing fails the 'as its neighbours are' check: the new test hard-codes the refusal text instead of using the shared Duplicate helper in tests/integration/duplicates.py (Duplicate.refusal, BY_INVOICE and BY_BILL at test_return_drafts.py:34-35), which every other duplicate-refusal test uses. Because of that I don't accept the commits as they stand.

commits: 0106c1d test: a JWKS key PyJWK rejects with a TypeError and a too-deep JWKS body count as an unusable key and a failed fetch
2a26965 fix: a JWKS key of the wrong shape is skipped and a too-deep JWKS body counts as a failed fetch
fixed.red: The branch auto/code-unit-auth did not exist, so I started from origin/main (88e55be). I added two cases to existing tests. The first is a new parameter of test_an_unusable_key_doesnt_hide_the_keys_after_it: a key with alg ["RS256"] placed before the signer's good key. The second is a new parameter of test_a_failed_jwks_fetch_logs_why: a 200 response whose body is b"[" * 200_000 (under MAX_JWKS_BYTES), with the expected reason "RecursionError". That reason is the JSON error's type, which REQ-002-PRS-NF008's table allows. I ran `uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_auth.py` on the unchanged code and both cases failed. The first raised `TypeError: cannot use 'list' as a dict key` from PyJWK in JwksCache._fetch, so the good key was never used. The second raised `RecursionError: Stack overflow ... while decoding a JSON array` instead of KeysUnavailable, and no jwks line was written. After the fix both pass, and so do the full suite (1577 passed), ruff check, ruff format --check, basedpyright and mdformat --check.
fixed.notes: The fix is in src/enterich/auth.py. _fetch now also skips a key when PyJWK raises TypeError, not only PyJWTError. _refresh now also catches RecursionError, so it writes the jwks line with outcome failed and reason RecursionError, and the request ends in KeysUnavailable (503). ruff format rewrote the per-key handler without parentheses as `except jwt.PyJWTError, TypeError:`, which is valid on the project's Python 3.14 (PEP 758). I also added a line under Unreleased/Fixed in CHANGELOG.md. No spec changed.

review.reason:
I redid the red check in my own worktree. At 0106c1d (the test: commit), `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_auth.py` gave 2 failed and 75 passed. The two failures are exactly the new cases: test_an_unusable_key_doesnt_hide_the_keys_after_it[broken1] and test_a_failed_jwks_fetch_logs_why[response4-RecursionError], the second failing with a RecursionError from json/decoder.py. At 2a26965 (the fix: commit) all 77 pass. I removed the worktree afterwards.

Do the tests check what the finding says is missing? Yes, through behaviour a caller sees.
- tests/unit/test_auth.py:285-296: a key with `alg: ["RS256"]` sits before the signer's good key, and verify_token must accept a token signed with the good key. So the good key is no longer thrown away.
- tests/unit/test_auth.py:394: a body of `b"[" * 200_000` must raise KeysUnavailable and write exactly one jwks line with outcome failed and reason RecursionError. That is the missing jwks line and the 503 the finding asks for.

Do they repeat or stray from their neighbours? No. Both are new parameters of the existing tests named in the verdict, so they repeat nothing and look like the cases around them.

Is the fix inside the specs? Yes. REQ-002-PRS-NF008's log table (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:214) allows "the type of a transport or JSON error" as the reason, and RecursionError is the type of the JSON error here.

Is the change limited to the finding? Yes.
- src/enterich/auth.py:103 adds RecursionError to the exceptions _refresh catches.
- src/enterich/auth.py:137 skips a key on TypeError as well as on PyJWTError. Written without parentheses, which is valid on Python 3.14 (PEP 758) and is what ruff format produces.
- CHANGELOG.md has one Unreleased/Fixed line citing REQ-002-PRS-NF008.
No spec, ADR or other file changed.
